geo.clue: A giant scramble crossing outside one of the world’s busiest stations.
geo.fact: Shibuya Crossing in Tokyo. Every light change, people cross from all directions at once.

geo.clue: A huge red gate that seems to float on the sea at high tide.
geo.fact: The torii of Itsukushima Shrine on Miyajima island, Hiroshima Prefecture.

geo.clue: Wild monkeys soaking in a steaming hot spring among the snow.
geo.fact: Jigokudani Snow Monkey Park in Nagano. The macaques bathe to stay warm in winter.

geo.clue: An active volcano smoking just across the bay from the city.
geo.fact: Sakurajima faces Kagoshima city and erupts small plumes regularly.

geo.clue: Neon signs and a famous running-man billboard along a canal.
geo.fact: Dotonbori in Osaka, famous for its signs and street food like takoyaki.

geo.clue: Japan’s highest mountain reflected in a calm lake at dawn.
geo.fact: Mt Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi, Yamanashi. Fuji sits on the Shizuoka and Yamanashi border.

geo.clue: A city park filled with giant snow sculptures every February.
geo.fact: The Sapporo Snow Festival takes over Odori Park each winter.

geo.clue: Tiny open-air food stalls light up the riverside at night.
geo.fact: Fukuoka’s yatai stalls in Nakasu serve ramen and grilled skewers.

kanji.fact: 地 means ground and 震 means shake.
The horse radical 馬 is a hint: old post stations kept horses.
紅 is crimson and 葉 is leaf. Also read momiji, the maple.
天 is sky or heaven and 気 is spirit or air.
電 is electricity and 車 is vehicle: an electric car.
The tree radical 木 sits on the left of 桜.
Three flowing lines: one of the oldest picture kanji.
Three peaks. Fujisan is 富士山.
